stem: This excerpt describes an instance of deportation during the 1930s as part of a repatriation effort. Why did the federal government implement repatriation?

options.label: F
options.text: To fulfill the terms of a global peace treaty

options.label: J
options.text: To prevent communist influence on labor unions

visual_elements: "They wanted us out of the country. I didn’t understand why when we’d been born here." . . . Emilia Castaneda was born in Los Angeles of Mexican parents. In 1935, she and her father and brother were forced to board a train bound for Mexico. —Linda Pressly, "U.S. Mexicans Haunted by Repatriation," BBC News, November 29, 2006
